Server-only Iroh fixed-path extension, 2026-11-09

Origin: https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh, package iroh 1.4.1.
Registry archive SHA256:
e3689cab508af9bcef7816c1201b403595ec6aa20e7d15e1f9683bb4be4a5b17
Published .cargo_vcs_info.json commit:
d6c6963b9602d1b8dd2ba53b6519e7eb19cc7940, path_in_vcs=iroh.
Complete published source, Cargo.toml.orig, README, MIT and Apache-2.0
licenses and upstream notices are retained. No upstream copyright changed.
This is visibly modified upstream Rust, not a new release or independent Noq.

Modified upstream files: src/endpoint/quic.rs, src/socket.rs and
src/socket/remote_map/remote_state.rs only.
Adds QuicTransportConfigBuilder::fixed_path(). At build, after all ordinary
setters, it disables QNT, multipath, server handshake migration and observed
address reports. The immutable config carries this policy into BOTH initial
server-config creation and ServerConfigBuilder::set_transport_config, which
disable ordinary migration. No raw Noq handle is exposed. Unselected configs
retain upstream behavior. Noq 1.4.0 and the existing reviewed Noq source are
unchanged; this calls its existing public configuration APIs.

The remote actor also selects each non-multipath connection's own path zero,
rather than projecting a peer-global preferred tuple from an older connection.
Without this, a new handshake over a changed socket has no selected public
path while the previous blackholed connection remains retained. New admission
would fail closed, making ordinary same-identity reconnection unusable. This
correction neither moves old paths nor admits changed-address frames.

Noq early_discard_packet rejects a changed remote before application-frame
processing when peer_may_probe is false. That condition requires disabling
ordinary migration AND negotiated QNT. Multipath and handshake migration must
also be disabled to prevent alternate initial or additional paths. Cached
Iroh path snapshots remain additional conservative checks, not the boundary
that enforces this policy. No network-address getter polling is introduced.

API implication: fixed-path is an additive, server-selected opt-in. It does
not support path migration, QNT, relay fallback or NAT traversal. A client
whose path changes must make a new connection and undergo new admission.
Rejected packets do not necessarily produce a wire-visible close; a timeout
is not proof of closure or resource return. Normal unchanged-path bounded
idle/write lifetimes and explicit joined shutdown remain in force.

Selection: only the root SERVER Cargo.toml patch uses this directory.
Independent Apple/Android/universal/client manifests, locks and vendor bytes
are unchanged. No global registry/cache edits. The root keeps the one
existing reviewed noq-proto path; no second Noq implementation is introduced.

Maintenance: on any Iroh/Noq update, recheck early rejection order, migration
and extension negotiation, both server-config construction paths, config
clone/replacement behavior and the encrypted two-direction physical-socket
regression with 8/16/16 MiB windows and original five-second observation.
Keep exact upstream/modified manifests, archive hash and licenses with imports.
Official API references:
https://docs.rs/noq/1.4.0/noq/struct.ServerConfig.html#method.migration
https://docs.rs/noq/1.4.0/noq/struct.TransportConfig.html
